summary: D. Dennis Hudson worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University around 1963-1970 and served as a Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College from 1970 to 2000.
D. H. Gordon was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Wellington College around 1909-1914 and at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst in 1914.

D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (circa 1927-1932). He held a post at the University of Mysore from circa 1932 to 1962 and taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, D. N. Dimri studied at Doon University. Dimri interned at WWF-India, was a fellow at UEEC, worked as Director (Publications) at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2016), and researched at University of Pannonia (2018-2019).

D. N. Shukla was an Indologist who earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer. Shukla held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, attested in 1958.

D. Neil Schmid specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he was a doctoral student supervised by Victor H. Mair.
D. R. Nagaraj was an Indologist who studied at Bangalore University and subsequently held a post there from around 1979 to 1998. He also taught Sheldon Pollock.
D. S. Subbaramaiya was a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.
D. Srinivasachar was an Indology scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore, both attested from 1931 to 1933.

Dagfinn Føllesdal is a philosopher and linguist. Educated at the University of Oslo and Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine, he taught at Harvard, the University of Oslo (circa 1967-1999), and Stanford University (1968-2011), and taught Bimal Krishna Matilal.

Dagmar Schwerk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her degrees, including a PhD under Dorji Wangchuk, at the University of Hamburg, held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of British Columbia (2018-2022), and became Professor at Leipzig University in 2024.

Dagmar Wujastyk specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. She served as a Principal Investigator at the University of Vienna in 2015 and became an Associate Professor at the University of Alberta in 2018.

Dagpo Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche. His students include David Seyfort Ruegg, Anne-Marie Blondeau, Thoupten Phuntshog, and Marie-Stella Boussemart.

Daichi Tado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Tado served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2020) and as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (2020-2026) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (2026).

Daiei Kaneko was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University under Manshi Kiyozawa. He founded Koho Gakuen and held posts at Otani University (circa 1916-1951) and Toyo University (circa 1928-1944).
Daigo Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. In 2006, Sasaki was attested as both a research student and holding a research student post at Ryukoku University.

Daijaku Judith Kinst is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She served as a faculty member at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from circa 1996 to 2007. Sasaki served as a lecturer and faculty member at Taisho University and as a regular lecturer at Chisan Denpōin.

Daijō Tokiwa was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Tokyo University under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, founded the Koa Buddhist Culture Research Institute, and taught Reimon Yuki.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University, training under Daicho Hayashi and Ekō Hashimoto. He founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and Hokyoji, served at Zenshuji Soto Mission, and was interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center.
